mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) indicates strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in expansionary periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE spikes do not correlate with subsequent economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO declines do not correlate with subsequent negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that typically leads to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS > 4.5% does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: When both Real Final Sales (RSAFS) and Housing Starts (HOUST) increase by more than 2% month-over-month, it signals a strong demand environment that boosts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both increase > 2% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint increase in RSAFS and HOUST does not correlate with subsequent positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, which typically supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of low UNRATE and high PAYEMS does not correlate with subsequent positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary easing cycle, a decrease in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% signals increased liquidity and lower borrowing costs, which typically boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decreases during easing cycles do not correlate with subsequent positive returns.
